title: Is the Pied Piper About a Real Historic Tragedy?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant examine the Pied Piper of Hamelin legend and whether it reflects a real event in the town of Hamelin (Hamlin), Germany, in 1284, when 130 children disappeared. They walk through the Grimm-style tale (rat infestation, unpaid piper, flute-led children into a mountain cave), the early documentary evidence (a lost stained glass window, the Lüneburg manuscript, Hamelin's dating inscriptions), and competing theories: the bubonic plague, Huntington's disease, a Children's Crusade, the Ostsiedlung eastward migration, child abandonment, and mass death or sacrifice. The episode also covers the town's street without music, the rats musical, and a listener mail segment on Kinderfest-style coming-of-age traditions and the term Latinx.

segments.title: Opening banter and fairy tale setup
segments.summary: Hosts joke around, introduce the episode as a fairy tale edition, recall earlier fairy tale episodes, and frame the Pied Piper as a tale that may be based on a real event.

segments.title: The Pied Piper tale and rat infestation
segments.summary: The hosts retell the Grimm-style tale: Hamelin is overrun by rats after the cats died, the piper (pied meaning multicolored clothing) offers to rid the town for a price, lures rats into the Weser River, and is then denied his payment.

segments.title: Revenge and the children's disappearance
segments.summary: The piper vows revenge and returns, playing his flute to lure about 130 children up a mountain to a cave that closes behind them. Versions differ on who survives, with one child who could not hear or keep up as the survivor.

segments.title: The 1284 stained glass window and early documentary evidence
segments.summary: The hosts describe the town church stained glass window that commemorated the event, the Lüneburg manuscript about a piper, and Hamelin's later dating inscriptions counting from the year 1284, which support the event as possibly real.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Break taken between the historical evidence and the theories section.

segments.title: Theories about what happened
segments.summary: Proposed explanations are discussed: bubonic plague (with the rats added later by Count Froben Christoph von Zimmern), Huntington's disease (judged unlikely), a Children's Crusade, the eastward Ostsiedlung migration to Transylvania, and child abandonment due to poverty.

segments.title: Town traditions, guilt, and mass death theories
segments.summary: The hosts describe Hamelin's street where music and dancing are banned, the town's tourism around the legend and the musical Rats, and Michael Rosen and Michael Boyer's view that the rats were a later addition. They speculate about guilt and a possible mass grave or mass death.

segments.title: Peru child sacrifice discovery
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the discovery of a mass child sacrifice in Peru, involving hundreds of children killed in a single day, as a comparison to the idea of a mass death in Hamelin.

segments.title: Wrap-up and show plug
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up, point listeners to the website for more on the Pied Piper, and move to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail on Kinderfest and Latinx
segments.summary: Listener Alexandra from Puerto Rico praises the Quinceañera episode and clarifies Latinx pronunciation and meaning. Listener Tiban Plinsky adds notes on Latinx pronunciation and backlash to the term, and the hosts give social media contact information.
